chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from one of those who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If wine or an intoxicating nabidh touches your garment, then wash it if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it. If you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer).
And by this isnad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Khayrān al-Khādim, who said:

I wrote to the man asking him about a garment that wine and pork meat touch: may one pray in it or not? For indeed our companions have differed regarding it. So he wrote: “Do not pray in it, for it is impure.”

key_terms.ثَوْبَكَ: your garment; the clothing affected by impurity
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine; a ritually impure intoxicant mentioned as contaminating the garment
key_terms.رِجْسٌ: impure; describing the contaminant as ritually filthy
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat (prayer); the prayer that must be repeated if performed in the impure garment
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it; the legal instruction to purify the garment
key_terms.لَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pork meat; a source of impurity mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.نَبِيذٌ مُسْكِرٌ: an intoxicating nabidh; any fermented drink causing intoxication in this context

ai.seo_question: What should be done if wine or pork contaminates clothing before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on garments contaminated by wine, intoxicating nabidh, or pork. It instructs that the affected area must be washed, or the whole garment if the exact place is unknown, and that salat (prayer) performed in such a garment must be repeated. It also explicitly forbids praying in a garment touched by such impurity because it is regarded as impure.
